deploymentEvidence.evidence: Archived official Deployment Addresses documentation explicitly states Ethereum mainnet and lists this StabilityPool under mkUSD, separately from ULTRA pool 0x6953504F2f4537D7a7B4024508f321f7816BB6ED. Its mkUSD DebtToken, PrismaCore, factory, liquidation manager and DAO PrismaVault rows match exact deployment constructor arguments. Table values were extracted from archived HTML/hydration content because reader output omitted table cells. Exact-address explorer attributes creator to Prisma Finance: Deployer; source service reports direct non-proxy deployment. No fresh runtime identity claim.

abiEvidence.evidence: Full original exact-address deployment ABI is retained, including constructor and events, with all 41 function entries inventoried. Selected fragments preserve exact input/output names, types and mutability. Address-bound deployed StabilityPool plus SafeERC20/Address, PrismaOwnable, SystemStart and exact immutable debt token/vault sources were inspected; no generic Liquity or ULTRA interface was substituted. Service labels match are not relabeled exact_match.

operationalEvidence.scope: Exit-only legacy principal/checkpoint and stored-collateral claims; neither deposits nor historical PRISMA claims selected. No new per-function financial gate.

notices.evidence: Official successor Resupply article links passed PIP-46 and confirms Prisma shutdown; Phase 1 debt ceilings zero, emissions to cease 2025-01-02; Phase 3 targeted 2025-01-10 boost calculator zero and forfeiture of unclaimed PRISMA. These were announced actions; this review does not attest the implementation/execution of every phase.

Official Resupply governance describes Prisma as now-defunct and ownership transferred to Resupply. Proposal aims to deprecate mkUSD/ULTRA PSM liquidity and recover crvUSD; not represented here as proof of proposal execution or as an exit path for pool deposits.
Supplementary shutdown implementer account distinguishes ULTRA StabilityPool repeated-claim bug from mkUSD. It is not used as deployment/ABI binding or a security endorsement.

linkReview.evidence: Official repository remains retrievable and links former Prisma docs. Direct former homepage https://www.prismafinance.com/, docs root and deployment path could not connect; governance PIP-46 retrieval also failed. No conclusion of squatting is asserted from network failure. Use attributable surviving official source repository as directory reference, not an unverified or presumed operating historical frontend.

debtToken.evidence: Bound DebtToken source sendToSP permits only immutable stabilityPoolAddress and _transfers specified sender tokens without ERC20 allowance; pool always supplies msg.sender. returnFromPool permits pool/trove managers and pool withdrawal passes address(this), msg.sender, capped amount. ERC20 default decimals is 18; ordinary direct transfer to pool is rejected, so direct mkUSD transfer is not a deposit. No approval/permit capability is added.

rewardVault.evidence: Fixed vault constructor binds Prisma token, locker, voter and this mkUSD pool as emission ID 0. Pool issuance invokes allocateNewEmissions(0); vault account registration, schedule and active status govern allocation. emissionSchedule and boostCalculator are owner-replaceable; claim transfer uses claimant own boost with address(0) boost delegate, then transfers PRISMA or locks in fixed locker depending mutable lockWeeks. Historical reward claims are excluded and no current emission/boost configuration is asserted.

collateralRegistry.evidence: No caller-selected collateral contract address or opaque execution payload. claimCollateralGains resolves caller indexes through collateralTokens and uses SafeERC20.safeTransfer; enableCollateral only factory, startCollateralSunset only core owner. Registry is not immutable: after 180-day sunset, factory can overwrite a slot and reset global sums; pending stored gains and token mapping must not be presumed immutable. Current full registry, token code and balances are not attested.

notes: Inherited comments mention frontend tags and automatic reward payout, but callable code has no frontend-tag parameter and deposit/withdraw only accrue collateral and PRISMA; ABI and actual code govern this record.
Stored gains are zeroed before collateral transfer in this mkUSD deployment. No ULTRA-specific bug conclusion or safety assurance is transplanted.
Loss accounting deliberately rounds loss up and rounds compounded entitlement down; liquidation can deplete principal fully.
No constructor, event, fallback or receive capability is created. There is no delegated-operator setter, permit/signature entry, arbitrary execute or multicall in this ABI.

selectedFunctions.label: Prisma mkUSD legacy StabilityPool withdraw/checkpoint
warnings: Legacy Ethereum mkUSD StabilityPool only, not the separate ULTRA pool, a TroveManager, PSM, rewards vault or Resupply product. Official successor notices confirm Prisma shutdown; this is exit/accounting metadata, not an operating yield offering. New deposits and historical PRISMA reward claims are not selected.

withdrawFromSP uses caller-owned mkUSD deposit units (18 decimals), not transferable shares. It returns min(requested amount, remaining compounded deposit) to msg.sender; liquidation losses can reduce this to zero. An amount at least the compounded deposit requests full exit. Zero amount checkpoints collateral and PRISMA accrual but still requires a recorded nonzero initial deposit and a timestamp later than the last deposit.

Deposits are consumed pro rata by liquidations across supported collateral types. P/S/G epoch-scale accounting and pool-favoring loss rounding apply; a prior-epoch deposit, two-scale decline or residual below one billionth of initial deposit is treated as zero. No principal, collateral-value or peg guarantee is implied.

withdrawFromSP accrues collateral gains and PRISMA bookkeeping but transfers neither reward class. claimCollateralGains only transfers caller gains already stored at supplied collateral indexes; it does not accrue/checkpoint fresh gains. When eligible, withdrawFromSP(0) checkpoints without withdrawing principal; a completed exit also leaves stored collateral gains claimable.

claimCollateralGains pays explicit recipient from caller entitlement using configured collateralTokens[index], not arbitrary caller-supplied contracts or calldata. Choose intended nonzero recipient and valid current indexes. Empty/duplicate indexes do not discover additional rewards; invalid indexes or failing token transfers can revert the call. No automatic redemption of collateral into ETH, mkUSD or crvUSD occurs.

The collateral array is factory-managed, not an immutable asset whitelist. Owner can sunset a collateral, and factory can reuse its slot after 180 days, reset its global sums and replace its token. Caller must resolve the current index-to-token mapping; historical collateral attribution is not a current mapping, claim-value or token-safety guarantee.

All selected functions are nonpayable and require zero native ETH. No signature, delegated-account management, arbitrary execution target, callback payload or multicall is admitted. Recipient and financial choices remain caller responsibilities under independent controls; catalog membership grants no additional authority.

Withdrawal has no PRISMA_CORE.paused check, unlike new deposits, but it triggers reward issuance through immutable PrismaVault. Vault registration, mutable emissions schedule and other dependency state can still cause exits/checkpoints to revert. Collateral transfers depend on configured token behavior. No live pause, configuration, balances, liquidity, backing or successful-execution claim is made.

The official 2024-12-30 transition notice scheduled emissions cessation for 2025-01-02 and boost-zero forfeiture of unclaimed PRISMA for Phase 3. Do not infer payable rewards from stored accounting or claimableReward: historical pool claimReward clears entitlement before calling vault, whose boost calculator can reduce payout to zero and whose lockWeeks can lock instead of transfer tokens. No current reward entitlement or phase-execution attestation is made.

A 2025 shutdown account reports an ULTRA-pool repeated-claim bug; that is a different deployment. This reviewed mkUSD source zeros stored collateral gains before safeTransfer. This narrow source observation is not a security audit or assurance about either pool.

Source-service creation/runtime match labels are preserved as match, not exact_match. Review binds ABI/source evidence to the exact deployment but is not a fresh runtime bytecode/dependency check or financial-safety assertion. Existing exact grants, canonical ABI/value validation, pauses, simulations and signing/execution boundaries remain authoritative.
